title: National Human Rights Commission Act (2009)
text:
Unofficial translation
The 8th Session
The National Human Rights Commission Act, 2009
In accordance with the provisions of the Interim National Constitution of the Republic
of the Sudan 2005, be it hereby passed by the National Assembly and signed by the
President of the Republic the following Act:
Chapter I
Preliminary Provisions
Title and Commencement
1- This Act shall be cited as the “National Human Rights Commission Act, 2009, and
shall come into force as from the date of signature.
Repeal
2- The National Human Rights Commission Act, 2004, is hereby repealed.
Interpretation
3- In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires:
“Commission”: Means the National Human Rights Commission established under
Section (4) of this Act.
“Secretariat Means the Secretariat General of the Commission, established
General”: under section (16) of this Act.
“Human Rights”: Means the rights and freedoms provided for in the Interim
National Constitution, 2005, and in the international and regional
human rights instruments, ratified by the Sudan.
“Constitution”: Means the Interim National Constitution of the Republic of the
Sudan, 2005.
“Member”: Means a member of the Commission provided for under section
(6) (1) of this Act.
“Chairperson”: Means the Chairperson of the Commission provided for under
Section (6) (3) of this Act.
Deputy Chairperson Means the Deputy Chairperson of the Commission provided for
under Section (6) (3) of this Act.
Chapter II
The Commission
Establishment and Head Office
4- (1) there shall be established under this Act a commission, to be known as the
“National Human Rights Commission”.
(2) The Head Office of the Commission shall be in the National Capital. It may
establish branches in all states of the Sudan.
Independence of the Commission
5- The Commission shall be independent in the performance of its duties and
functions, in its decision-making and in the managing of its finances.

Unofficial translation
Composition and Membership
6- (1) The Commission shall be composed of fifteen members appointed by the
President of the Republic after consultations at the Presidency and obtainment of
the approval of the First Vice President, taking into consideration in their
appointment representation of women and civil society organizations; provided that
the member satisfies the following criteria:
(a) Be of sound mind;
(b) Be of not less than twenty one (21) years of age;
(c) Be independent, competent, experienced, non-partisan and impartial;
(d) Be widely known for their commitment to human rights causes; and
(e) Has not been convicted of a crime involving honesty and moral turpitude.
(2) Membership of the Commission shall be for a period of five years subject to
renewal for one final term.
(3) The President of the Republic shall appoint, after consultations at the
Presidency and with the consent of the First Vice President, a Chairperson and a
Deputy Chairperson, provided that one of them shall be a woman.
(4) The Chairperson and his/her Deputy shall work on full time basis.
Vacancy of a Member’s Post
7- (1) The post of a member of the Commission shall fall vacant for any of the
following reasons:
(a) Mental infirmity or physical incapacity;
(b) Issue of a decision under section (2) of this Act;
(c) Acceptance of Member’s resignation;
(d) Death.
(2) Membership may lapse by a decision from the Presidency of the Republic for
any of the following reasons:
(a) Conviction of a crime involving honesty or moral turpitude;
(b) Repeated absence as stipulated by the Regulations.
(3) In case any post turns vacant for any of the reasons provided for in this
section, selection of the successor of such member shall be made following the
same procedure provided for under section (6) of this Act.
Oath
8- The members of the Commission shall take the following oath:
“I swear by Almighty Allah to carry out my duty as member to the National
Human Rights Commission with due integrity and sincerity without fear or
favoritism and Allah is my witness to this statement”.
Chapter III
Functions of the Commission, its Powers and Procedures
Functions of the Commission
9- (1) The Commission shall be competent to protect and strengthen human rights,
create awareness of human rights, publish the same and monitor the application of
the rights and freedoms enshrined in the Bill of Rights provided for in the
Constitution.
Page 2 of 7

Unofficial translation
(2) Without prejudice to the provisions of subsection (1), the Commission shall
have the following functions:
(a) to operate as a reference for information to the government, different
States organs concerned and civil society organizations working in the field
of human rights;
(b) to enlighten the public on human rights and the necessity to respect them
and to apply them by all bodies;
(c) Preparation of human rights studies and researches.
(d) to study any matter of a national nature relating to human rights, referred
thereto by the Government, or by the State organs, or by civil society
organizations and to make recommendations on the same;
(e) to provide advice to the government on any matter relating to human
rights, whether referred to it by the government or initiated on its own
motion;
(f) to prepare studies and initiate, through bodies concerned, bills, legislations
or decisions relating to human rights and to prepare reports and submit
recommendations on the same to the bodies concerned;
(g) to submit recommendations, proposals and reports to the government or to
the National Assembly, or to any other body concerning any matter relating
to human rights, including request to review legislative provisions or
administrative decisions to be in conformity with the basic principles of
human rights;
(h) to receive complaints from individuals and other bodies and to conduct
investigations thereon and to take the necessary measures in accordance
with the provisions of this Act or any other law and to recommend
appropriate remedies to the relevant body;
(i) to address competent authorities regarding any matter relating to any
violation of human rights and to request them to end such violation;
(j) to encourage the government to join international treaties, conventions and
agreements, on hum rights;
(k) to endeavor to harmonize national legislations and practices with human
rights standards;
(l) to prepare annual reports on the situation of human rights in the Sudan;
(m) to spread awareness of human rights among different sectors of the people
of the Sudan, through media, seminars, publications and any other means
of information;
(n) to cooperate with the United Nations and its specialized agencies, regional
organizations, human rights centers, non-governmental organizations and
any other similar organizations working in the field of human rights;
(o) to establish close relations with organizations which are active in the field of
human rights outside and inside the Sudan;
(p) to submit reports to the National Assembly on any specific matter
concerning human rights;
(q) to approve the organizational chart and terms and conditions of service of
employees of the Commission;
Powers of the Commission
10- (1) The Commission shall have the following powers:
(a) to look into complaints of human rights violations raised to it by individuals
or civil society organizations or by any other body to ascertain whether or
not there is violation of human rights and take appropriate measures;
Page 3 of 7

Unofficial translation
(b) to form committees, or task force groups or seek help of any person or any
entity on permanent or temporary basis, to assist in the discharge of its
responsibilities;
(c) to investigate with full freedom on any matter falling within its competence
whether referred to it by government or it decided on its own motion or
referred to it by some other body concerned with human rights causes;
(d) to address the public directly or through available means of information in
order to disseminate its opinions and recommendations, to all sectors of the
society;
(e) to coordinate with the Human Rights Commission in Southern Sudan and
other states on matters pertaining to fulfilling constitutional commitments in
relation to the human rights;
(f) to make internal regulations for the conduct of its business and procedure
of its meetings.
(2) Notwithstanding the provisions of sub-section (1) (a), the Commission may not
look into any complaint if the same is being hared by any competent court.
Procedures of the Commission
11- (1) Whenever the Commission decides that there is a violation of human rights on
the part of any public servant or any of the government or non-government
organizations, or any other body, the Commission may:
(a) recommend to the relevant government authorities to take the
appropriate measure for prompt reparations of the aggrieved person or to
publish its findings or to take any other appropriate measures as it deems
appropriate;
(b) provide the complainant or his representative, if they so requested, with a
copy of the summary of report of the investigation;
(2) The relevant government organs shall inform the Commission within sixty days
of the measures taken concerning the recommendations submitted to it under the
provisions of sub-section (1)(a).
(3) The Commission may request all government and non-government institutions
to provide any information concerning the extent of implementation of the Bill of
Rights enshrined in the Constitution, and to report on any derogation or deprivation
of these rights.
(4) Any statement made by any person before the Commission shall not be used
against them in any civil or criminal proceedings save when they are being tried for
perjury, provided that such statement:
(a) was made in reply to a question which the Commission asked them to
answer, or
(b) is related to the subject matter under investigation.
Meetings of the Commission
12- (1) The Commission shall meet once at least every month upon the invitation of its
Chairperson.
(2) The Commission may convene an extraordinary meeting at the invitation of the
Chairperson or at the request of one third of the members.
(3) The quorum for the meetings of the Commission shall be reached when more
than half of its members are present.
(4) Decisions shall be taken by a majority of votes of members present and in case
of a tie, the Chairperson shall have a casting vote.

Unofficial translation
Functions of the Chairperson
13- The Chairperson shall be the first responsible person for the Commission and shall
supervise all administrative and financial matters required for the Commission, and
without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing; the Chairperson shall have the
following functions:
(a) Chair the meetings of the Commission;
(b) Represent the Commission before others;
(c) Follow-up implementation of the decisions of the Commission;
(d) Forward to the Presidency of the Republic and the National Assembly,
periodical reports approved by the Commission concerning all matters
relating to human rights and any violation committed from time to time;
(e) Any other responsibilities which the Commission may assign to him.
Functions of the Deputy Chairperson
14- The Deputy Chairperson shall perform the functions of the Chairperson in their
absence as well as performing the functions delegated to them by the Chairperson.
Emoluments and Privileges of the Chairperson,
Deputy Chairperson and Members of the Commission
15- The Presidency of the Republic shall determine the emoluments of the
Chairperson, their Deputy and the entitlements of the members of the Commission.
Chapter IV
The Secretariat General and its Functions
Establishment of the Secretariat General
16- The Commission shall establish a Secretariat General headed by the Secretary
General and shall include such number of employees according to the approved
organizational chart to enable the Commission to perform its duties.
Functions of the Secretariat General
17- The Secretariat General shall be responsible for running the executive and
administrative work of the Commission and, without prejudice to the generality of
the foregoing, the Secretariat General shall have the following functions:
(a) execute decisions and directives of the Commission;
(b) prepare minutes of the meetings and deliberations;
(c) carry out necessary executive and administrative business of all permanent
and non-permanent specialized committees;
(d) prepare the annual budget of the Commission well in accordance with the
principles and standards adopted by the State and submit the same to the
Commission for approval and submission to the Presidency of the Republic
for endorsement;
(e) Prepare the Commission’s organizational chart, the conditions of service of
staff and submit them to the Commission.
(f) Undertake any other tasks assigned to it by the Commission or by the
Chairperson.
Chapter V
General Provisions
Page 5 of 7

Unofficial translation
Immunity of the Chairperson, their Deputy
And Members of the Commission
18- Save in cases of flagrante delicto, the Chairperson, their Deputy or any member of
the Commission shall not be arrested or have any criminal or civil proceedings
taken against them in connection with any work relating to the performance of
duties assigned to them under this Act except after obtaining written permission
from the Presidency of the Republic.
Participation of the Relevant Government Organs
19- The Council of Ministers shall appoint six representatives of the relevant
governmental organs to take part in the deliberations of the Commission in
advisory capacity.
Budget, Accounts, Subsidies, and Audit
20 (1) The Commission shall have an independent budget to be submitted to the
Presidency of the Republic for endorsement and shall be approved by the National
Assembly as part of the State consolidated annual budget;
(2) The Commission shall establish its own accounting unit to operate on the basis
of established accounting norms including the keeping of sound books on revenue
and expenditure;
(3) The Commission may receive national or foreign subsidies in accordance with
the guidelines laid down by the Presidency of the Republic;
(4) The national Audit Chamber or whoever it authorizes shall audit the accounts of
the Commission at the end of every fiscal year and evaluate its financial reports
and, forward the same to the National Assembly.
Power to Make Regulations
21- (1) Notwithstanding the provisions of the Financial and Accounting Procedures Act
(2007), the Commission may make the necessary regulations for the
implementation of the provisions of this Act. Such regulations may include
organization of the administrative, financial, and accounting matters, the
procedures of the business of the Commission and receiving and handling of
complaints.
(2) Notwithstanding the provisions of sub-section (1), the Commission may not
make regulations concerning terms and conditions of service of the employees of
the Commission or amicable settlement of claims of damage or any other matters
entailing financial obligations, except with the consent of the bodies concerned.

Testimony
I hereby certify that the National Assembly has approved the National Human Rights
Commission, 2009, in its 3rd meeting of the 8th session, on 25 Rabie Thani 1430 H,
corresponding to 21 April 2009 and; the Permanent Joint Committee of the two
Chambers has ruled, in its meeting No ( ) on ……….. 1430 H corresponding to ………..
2009, that this Act does not affect the interests of the states.
Ahmed Ibrahim al-Tahir
Speaker,
National Assembly
Chairperson,

I concur.
